title: Novel lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev-Petviashvili-I equation
abstract: We construct novel higher-order lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev-Petviashvili-I (mKP-I) equation by applying the generalized long-wave limit method with spectral perturbations. By tuning the phase parameters in the soliton solution, we obtain second- and third-order lump solutions, which, to the best of our knowledge, are reported here for the first time for the mKP-I equation. A detailed asymptotic analysis reveals that these degenerate lumps exhibit anomalous scattering analogous to that in the KP-I equation. However, in contrast to the KP-I case, no complete energy equipartition occurs after the collision, and the two lumps remain distinguishable in the subleading terms of their asymptotic amplitudes. This distinction highlights a difference in the interaction dynamics between the modified and standard KP-I equations.
summary: This paper constructs novel higher-order lump solutions for the mKP-I equation using advanced spectral perturbation methods. The research analyzes the anomalous scattering of these degenerate lumps, finding a crucial difference from standard KP-I: energy equipartition does not occur, and the interacting components remain distinguishable. This advances understanding of nonlinear wave dynamics in integrable systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is constructing novel higher-order lump solutions for the modified Kadomtsev-Petviashvili-I (mKP-I) equation and analyzing their anomalous scattering behavior.
main_result: Novel second- and third-order lump solutions are found, demonstrating anomalous scattering where interacting lumps remain distinguishable in subleading terms, unlike the standard KP-I case.
method: The study employs the generalized long-wave limit method combined with spectral perturbations to derive these complex localized rational solutions.
model_or_system: The system is governed by the mKP-I equation, a $(2+1)$-dimensional integrable nonlinear evolution equation that models water waves with cubic nonlinearity.
key_observables: Asymptotic amplitudes and trajectories of interacting lump waves; spatial configuration of multiple lumps parameterized by constants like $C_{33}$ and $C_{35}$.
important_parameters: The order of the solution (second or third), and free parameters derived from tuning phase parameters in the N-soliton solution.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on parameterizing soliton solutions and making specific simplifications for higher orders, such as setting certain coefficients to zero.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the evolution of a second-order lump; Figure 2 illustrates anomalous scattering with three lumps; Figure 3 demonstrates how varying parameters ($C_{33}, C_{35}$) changes the spatial arrangement of six lumps at $t=0$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically constructs solutions using advanced methods, analyzes their long-time asymptotic behavior (scattering), and contrasts the interaction dynamics between mKP-I and KP-I equations.
why_interesting: While focused on classical integrable systems, the study of anomalous scattering and energy non-equipartition in nonlinear PDEs provides mathematical tools relevant to understanding complex wave interactions in quantum field theories or many-body dynamics where integrability is key.

Figure 3 illustrates how the parameters C33 and C35 affect the spatial configuration of the six lumps at t = 0. In the ground state (C33 = C35 = 0), the solution exhibits only three peaks, indicating that the six lumps are not fully separated. As C33 increases while the other parameters remain fixed, the six individual lumps gradually decouple and self-organize into a triangular structure. In contrast, when C35 becomes large, the six lumps decouple into a different arrangement: one lump remains near the origin, while the remaining five are evenly distributed on a circle around it, forming a regular pentagon.
